scope: Read-only diagnosis of first Knowledge request after validated startup; no backend changes authorized or made
result: Derived projection/replay rebuild is not present on an unchanged first post-startup read. Public-payload copying/HTTP serialization is tens of milliseconds locally. Two sequential fresh remote proof requests and cold connection/proxy overhead remain the concrete latency candidates; current production phase costs are not measured here.
source_findings: hosted_app_v1.startup calls controller.knowledge.learning_view before readiness. AutonomousKnowledge._read retains its projection, including learning_replay, in _projection_cache; discarding the returned deepcopy does not discard that internal cache.

Every current read still executes knowledge_snapshot, journal/schema proof, full cached-row/descriptor validation, source/schema proof, and admission checks before consulting the derived projection identity. Warm cache authority is not head-only.
For identical fully validated inputs, first and repeated post-startup calls reuse _project and _learning_replay output. Each still copies compact inputs/output and FastAPI serializes the response.

The present warm path sends the full journal/schema proof and final source/schema proof in two sequential read_snapshot requests. The source proof is intentionally after local source validation. There is no duplicate learning-view/projection build on that path.

public_dto.exact_existing_projection_6064_equality: versions, uses, quarantined and learning_replay all equal

tiny_native_fixture.fixture: Existing MockHrana plus the existing two-intake native-proof fixture pattern. Supported journal injection uses the existing hosted JOURNAL_SCHEMA; native reducer, validators, all-column typed proofs and transport code run unchanged.

recommendation.priority: Assess one final combined atomic proof request for an exact fully validated cache hit; retain existing cold and mutation paths
recommendation.soundness: Sound in principle if local cached-row/state/source-byte validation completes first and both complete typed journal and source/schema/roster proofs then match in one fresh final read_snapshot before any cached payload is released. This preserves every-read authority checks and gives one coherent remote certificate after local validation while removing one sequential HTTP request. It is not implemented or validated by this diagnosis.
recommendation.reuse_available: read_snapshot already supports multiple bounded SELECTs in one BEGIN/COMMIT/close request; _schema_query, _proof_query, _proof_expected and _proof_matches already encode the needed exact checks. The new work is coordinating proof construction, validation and cache admission, not changing transport limits or adding a service.
mandatory_conditions: Capture the existing admitted immutable complete journal cache and exact source roster; validate local cached originals/descriptors/state under existing ordered locks before constructing the final certificate. No cache admission or caller exposure may precede the certificate.

Include complete native journal and source schemas, every authority column and explicit storage type, full ordered rosters, N+1/count/length/root checks for all source batches, not just heads or source descriptors.
Compare against the exact originally certified local bytes/state and return only an exact matching derived payload. An unchanged head alone is never sufficient.

Missing or evicted bytes, absent admitted caches, schema changes, journal changes and source mismatches must discard the candidate and preserve existing full bounded collection/reducer/raw-source/final-proof behavior. Preserve the existing fail-closed corruption behavior rather than silently replacing a failed source proof with a success from a fallback.

Respect the unchanged 128-SELECT snapshot bound, existing source batch bounds, byte limit/deadline and no-retry behavior. Combined schemas/journal consume extra SELECT slots; use the unchanged existing path when the combined request cannot fit.

Hold appropriate existing ordered summary/source locks through captured expected-byte identity, final proof checks and cache admission. Mutation after prefetch or before final certification must still fail; no partial cursor/payload can escape an uncertain transaction.

Focused adversarial verification remains necessary: same-head earlier-row changes, all source byte/roster/schema mutations, post-prefetch/final-boundary changes, cache eviction, accepted-stream disappearance/regression, concurrent claims/Knowledge ordering, protocol failure, and returned-object alias isolation.
recommendation.serialization_option: No further precomputation is warranted by this profile: derived projection/replay already warms at startup. A JSON-byte cache would save about 12ms of measured encoding/render work on this older public payload while adding invalidation complexity; it does not target the observed second-scale variation.
recommendation.expected_limit: One fewer proof round trip may materially improve latency. Neither this profile nor that change can guarantee universal <=1s across fresh client TLS, proxy/worker cold starts and variable database latency.

mac_measurement_that_distinguishes_cause: Use matched read-only direct-backend and Sites-proxy requests for the same deployment and unchanged head set, with fresh-client and reused-client variants. Retain DNS, connect, TLS, TTFB and total times; alternate order so one route does not always pay the cold start.

Retain route-entry, journal-proof, local-validation, source-proof and response-serialization durations with fixed phase labels only. These reveal whether a slow request is in database proofs, Python processing or before backend entry. No tokens, SQL parameters, headers or bodies belong in such logs.

Direct and proxy both slow with proof durations high implicates backend/database connections. Proxy slow while matched direct/backend phase timings remain stable implicates the Sites hop. A measured TLS/connect component distinguishes client cold connection time; subtracting it alone still leaves proxy/backend/proof time unresolved.

negative_acceptance_preserved.source: Coordinator/Mac reports, not this worker's network measurements
